rounds.text: Omax Autos Ltd trades at an attractive P/E multiple of 10.7x and a price-to-book value of 1.26x, while offering a dividend yield of 2.45% [E1, E2, E4]. The company exhibits robust fundamental momentum, demonstrated by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 25% and an impressive trailing twelve-month profit growth of 188% [E15, E21]. Operational efficiency is also improving, with operating margins expanding to 11% in TTM from 7% three years earlier, supported by an increasing yearly operating-margin trend over the last seven years [E30, E32]. Balance sheet health is remarkably strong, featuring debt-to-equity of 0.15x alongside a reduction in borrowings to Rs 53 Cr in Mar 2026 and robust free cash flow of Rs 66 Cr [E36, E38, E39]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over 10 years is -7% [E14], and the median return on equity over the last 10 years stands at -2% [E26].

Omax Autos Ltd carries significant underlying profitability and historical earnings quality risks that the headline P/E multiple obscures [E6, E9]. Long-term top-line erosion is evident in the 10-year compounded sales growth of -7% [E14], while historical return on equity has been severely depressed, showing a 10-year median ROE of -2% [E26] and a 5-year median ROE of -1% [E27]. Furthermore, structural profitability struggles are highlighted by an exceptionally weak ROA of 0.06% [E8] and a low 3-year average ROE of 4.98% [E63]. Balance sheet and earnings integrity are further compromised by substantial contingent liabilities of Rs 137 Cr [E64] and an earnings profile bloated by Rs 32.7 Cr of other income [E65], alongside a high cost of borrowing [E66]. The stock also exhibits extreme historical volatility of 56.6% [E54] and a catastrophic worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -90.8% [E53]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong recent momentum with a 5-year profit growth CAGR of 21% [E61], an operating cash flow of Rs 67 Cr backed by a cash conversion ratio of 1.81x [E34, E35], and a discounted cash flow model pointing to an intrinsic value of Rs 768 per share [E45].

Conceded: [E6, E9, E14, E26, E27, E53, E54, E64, E65, E66]. However, the bear's emphasis on past struggles ignores extraordinary fundamental acceleration, including a TTM sales growth of 32% [E17] and a staggering 188% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21]. This robust operational turnaround is fully backed by real liquidity rather than accounting fiction, evidenced by a massive operating cash flow of Rs 67 Cr and a cash conversion ratio of 1.81x in March 2026 [E34, E35]. Balance sheet risk is actively being unwound as borrowings dropped significantly from Rs 77 Cr to Rs 53 Cr [E39], while operating margins expand to 11% [E30]. Market participants are severely mispricing this transformation, with a reverse DCF implying that the current price demands an absurd -0.3% earnings growth [E47] against an actual intrinsic valuation of Rs 768 per share [E45], leaving a massive margin of safety of 73.4% [E46].

Conceded: [E17, E21, E34, E35, E39, E47]. The bull's highlighted operational turnaround is built upon a fragile and heavily distorted foundation, as reported earnings explicitly include a massive other income of Rs. 32.7 Cr [E65], proving that recent profit spikes are not solely from core automotive operations. Furthermore, the company carries a looming threat of contingent liabilities totaling Rs. 137 Cr [E64], which dwarfs current profitability metrics and remains completely unaccounted for in the bull's tidy DCF narrative. Long-term historical data completely undermines the thesis of a permanent structural shift, as compounded sales growth over a 10-year horizon sits at a dismal -7% [E14], and the 10-year median return on equity is a deeply negative -2% [E26]. While the bull points to reduced nominal borrowings [E39], the data provider explicitly flags that the company's cost of borrowing seems high [E66], creating sustained pressure on capital servicing. Finally, the extreme historical volatility of 56.6% [E54] and a catastrophic worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -90.8% [E53] demonstrate that this equity is an extremely hazardous vehicle prone to severe structural collapses regardless of short-term cash flow prints.
